issues.legal_issue: A bequest to a first beneficiary is limited to a life interest when the will gives later beneficiaries an absolute interest after the first beneficiary’s lifetime and that construction gives effect to both dispositions.
material_facts: The will provided that the testatrix’s eldest daughter would enjoy the movable property after the testatrix’s death and that, after the daughter’s lifetime, her male children would enjoy it permanently and with absolute rights.
The will used similar language elsewhere to create interests limited to a beneficiary’s lifetime, including one instance without an express prohibition on alienation.

The parties agreed that the will intended to confer an absolute and permanent interest on the daughter’s male children; construing the daughter’s interest as absolute would prevent that gift from taking effect.

The dispute arose in a suit for partition and separate possession, in which the competing claims depended on whether a court-sale purchaser acquired the daughter’s entire interest or only her life interest.
issues.conclusion: The daughter received only a life interest, and the absolute remainder was conferred on her male children. The appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 69, 72 and 73 of the Indian Succession Act, 1865, a will is read as a whole, reasonable meaning should be given to every part, and the same words ordinarily carry the same meaning throughout. Section 82 presumes that a bequest conveys the testator’s whole interest unless the will shows a restricted interest. Section 84 and its illustrations distinguish words that make later beneficiaries direct objects of an independent gift from words that merely describe the first taker’s interest; illustration (c) supports successive interests where the gift to the later beneficiaries follows the first taker’s death. A cardinal principle of will construction is to give effect, as far as legally possible, to every disposition and to avoid a construction that makes a later gift ineffective. The court noted that each will must be construed on its own terms and in the setting of its clauses, and found the cited authorities unhelpful as precedents for that task.

predicates.will_construction_case: The dispute concerns the construction of a will that disposes of property through successive interests.
predicates.later_beneficiaries_are_direct_gift_reci: The will gives later beneficiaries an independent interest in the property, rather than merely describing the extent of the first beneficiary’s interest.
predicates.later_gift_takes_effect_after_first_take: The will provides that the later beneficiaries’ interest takes effect after the first beneficiary’s lifetime.
predicates.life_interest_preserves_both_disposition: Treating the first beneficiary’s interest as lasting only for that beneficiary’s life allows both the first gift and the later gift to take effect.

issues.definition: When a will-construction case includes an independent gift to later beneficiaries taking effect after the first beneficiary’s lifetime, and a life interest for the first beneficiary preserves both dispositions, the first beneficiary has only a life interest.
